task_prompts.http-bc3b0441: When a HeaderMap's IntoIter is being dropped and one of the values it drops during cleanup panics, previously-yielded values can end up getting dropped a second time (this shows up as a double-free under Miri, e.g. with a custom Drop impl that frees a raw pointer). Reproduction: create a HeaderMap where one name has multiple appended values and another has a single value whose Drop panics; get an into_iter(), manually consume a couple of items with iter.next(), then drop the remaining iterator (catching the panic). The value(s) already taken out via next() end up being dropped again during the iterator's own drop cleanup. Dropping IntoIter should never cause values that were already yielded to be dropped again, even if a later value's Drop panics. Please fix this.
task_prompts.http-7767ff70: HeaderMap's iterators (iter, iter_mut, values, values_mut) can report an incorrect size_hint that overstates how many items remain by one, in maps where at least one header name has multiple appended values. For example, build a HeaderMap where header counts per name are like [3, 1, 2], then repeatedly call size_hint() and next() on headers.iter()/iter_mut()/values()/values_mut() while tracking how many items actually remain — the lower bound from size_hint() should never exceed the true remaining count, but it currently can be 1 too high in some states. Please fix size_hint() for these iterators so it always returns an accurate (non-overstated) bound as the iterator is consumed.
